title: Set 113

sentences.ko: 나 회사 얘기 2분만 해도 돼? 우리 팀에 한 명 있는데, 매번 오늘 안으로 주겠다고 해 놓고 금요일 오후에나 보내. 그것도 보내면 다행이고. 그래서 여섯 시까지 남아서 나가기 전에 그럴듯하게 손보는 건 나야. 그런데 다들 그 사람을 좋아해. 뭐든 다 하겠다고 하는 사람이니까.
sentences.text: Can I complain about work for two minutes? There's a guy on my team who tells me he'll have it to me by the end of the day, every single time, and then it shows up Friday afternoon, if it shows up at all. So I'm the one sitting there at six making it look finished before it goes out. And everybody loves him, because he's the one who says yes to everything.

alts.text: Mind if I vent about work for two minutes? This guy on my team swears he's gonna have it to me by end of day, every single time, and then it turns up Friday afternoon, if it turns up at all. So I'm the one stuck there at six making it look done before it goes out. And everyone thinks he's great, cause he's the guy who says yes to everything.

May I complain about work for two minutes? There is someone on my team who tells me he will have it to me by the end of the day, every single time, and then it arrives on Friday afternoon, if it arrives at all. So I am the one sitting there at six making it look finished before it goes out. And everyone thinks highly of him, because he is the one who says yes to everything.

sentences.note: **he'll have it to me by the end of the day** 는 오늘 퇴근 전까지 넘겨주겠다는 말이다. 뒤에 붙인 **if it shows up at all** 은 오기는 하면 다행이라는 뜻으로, 앞말을 비꼴 때 쓴다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 일요일에 언니가 꼬드겨서 그 스피닝 수업이란 걸 갔는데, 끝까지 다 따라갔거든. 그래서 나 괜찮은 줄 알았지. 그런데 월요일에 차에서 내리는데 소리를 안 내고는 못 내리겠더라. 무슨 대단한 일이라도 해낸 것처럼 만나는 사람마다 얘기하고 다니는데, 남은 거라고는 남들처럼 앉지도 못한다는 것뿐이야.
sentences.text: My sister talked me into one of those spin classes on Sunday, and I kept up the whole time, so I figured I was fine. Then Monday I couldn't get out of the car without making a noise. I've been telling everybody about it like I did something, and all I've got to show for it is I can't sit down like a normal person.

alts.text: So my sister dragged me to one of those spin classes Sunday, and I kept up the whole time, so I figured I was good. Then Monday I couldn't get out of the car without making a noise. I keep telling everyone about it like I did something, and the only thing I got out of it is I can't sit down like a normal person.

My sister persuaded me to attend one of those spin classes on Sunday, and I kept up the entire time, so I assumed I was fine. Then on Monday I could not get out of the car without making a noise. I have been telling everyone about it as though I accomplished something, and all I have to show for it is that I cannot sit down like a normal person.

sentences.note: **talked me into** 는 꼬드겨서 하게 만들었다는 뜻이다. **all I've got to show for it** 은 그 고생해서 얻은 게 이것뿐이라고 할 때 쓴다.

sentences.ko: 잠드는 건 문제가 아니야. 그건 괜찮아. 매일 새벽 네 시에 깨서는 누운 채로 잘 시간이 얼마나 남았나 계산하고 있는데, 바로 그것 때문에 잠이 더 안 와. 그러다 알람 울리기 한 이십 분 전에 겨우 다시 잠들어. 아내는 시계 좀 그만 보라고 하는데, 안 봐도 몇 시인지 알아.
sentences.text: Falling asleep isn't the problem, that part's fine. I'm up at four every morning, and then I lie there doing the math on how much time I've still got, which is exactly what keeps me awake. And about twenty minutes before the alarm I finally fall back asleep. My wife keeps telling me to stop looking at the clock, but I know what time it is anyway.

alts.text: Getting to sleep isn't the issue, that part's fine. I'm just up at four every morning, lying there counting up how much time I've still got, which is the exact thing keeping me awake. And like twenty minutes before the alarm I finally drop back off. My wife keeps saying quit looking at the clock, but I know what time it is anyway.

Falling asleep is not the problem; that part is fine. I wake at four every morning, and then I lie there calculating how much time I have left, which is precisely what keeps me awake. And about twenty minutes before the alarm I finally fall back asleep. My wife keeps telling me to stop looking at the clock, but I know what time it is regardless.

sentences.note: **doing the math** 는 머릿속으로 숫자를 따져 본다는 뜻이다. **fall back asleep** 은 깼다가 다시 잠드는 것을 말한다.

sentences.ko: 소파 들어온 지 3주 됐는데 아직도 마음에 드는지 모르겠어. 매장에서는 좋아 보였거든. 그런데 매장에는 티비가 없었잖아. 그래서 지금 우리 네 식구가 한 줄로 허리를 꼿꼿이 세우고 앉아서 무슨 순서 기다리는 사람들처럼 있어. 반품하려면 40달러 들고 계단으로 다시 내려야 해서, 그냥 이대로 사는 수밖에 없을 것 같아.
sentences.text: The couch got here three weeks ago and I still can't tell you if I like it. It looked great in the store, but there wasn't a TV in the store, so now the four of us are sitting straight up in a row like we're waiting to be called in for something. Sending it back is forty dollars and I'd have to get it down the stairs again, so I think we just live with it.

alts.text: We've had the couch three weeks and I still couldn't tell you if I like it. Looked great in the store, but there was no TV in the store, so now the four of us are sitting bolt upright in a row like we're waiting to get called in for something. Sending it back's forty dollars and I'd have to haul it down the stairs again, so I figure we just live with it.

The couch arrived three weeks ago and I still cannot tell you whether I like it. It looked wonderful in the store, but there was no television in the store, so now the four of us sit straight up in a row as though we are waiting to be called in for something. Returning it costs forty dollars and I would have to carry it down the stairs again, so I believe we will simply live with it.

sentences.note: **sitting straight up in a row** 는 한 줄로 허리를 꼿꼿이 세우고 앉은 모습이다. **live with it** 은 마음에 안 들어도 바꾸지 않고 그냥 참고 산다는 뜻이다.

sentences.ko: 내 폰이 이제 안 울려. 한 번 진동하고 바로 음성사서함으로 넘어가서, 누가 전화했다는 걸 한 시간 뒤에나 알게 돼. 무음도 아니야. 그건 마흔 번은 확인했어. 재시작하니까 하루는 괜찮다가 또 그러기 시작하더라. 그러니까 내가 안 받으면 그래서 그런 거야. 그냥 한 번 더 걸어 줘.
sentences.text: My phone won't ring anymore. It buzzes once and goes straight to voicemail, so I'm finding out an hour later that somebody called me. And it's not on silent, I've checked that about forty times. I restarted it and it was fine for a day, and then it started doing it again, so if I don't pick up, that's why. Just call again.

alts.text: So my phone's stopped ringing. It buzzes once then goes right to voicemail, so I find out an hour later that somebody called. And it's not on silent, I've checked that like forty times. I restarted it and it was fine for a day, then it started up again, so if I don't pick up, that's why. Just call again.

My phone no longer rings. It buzzes once and goes directly to voicemail, so I learn an hour later that someone has called me. And it is not on silent; I have checked that about forty times. I restarted it and it was fine for a day, and then it began doing it again, so if I do not answer, that is the reason. Please simply call again.

sentences.note: **goes straight to voicemail** 은 신호도 안 가고 바로 음성사서함으로 넘어간다는 말이다. **if I don't pick up** 의 pick up 은 걸려 온 전화를 받는다는 뜻이다.

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "There is a man on my team" 이 어색해서 "There is someone on my team" 으로 고쳤다. guy 를 man 으로 그대로 바꾼 티가 났다.
3번 casual 의 "adding up how much time I've still got" 은 원어민이 그 자리에 안 쓰는 말이라 "counting up" 으로 고쳤다.
4번 note 가 text 에 없는 표현(sitting bolt upright, casual 에만 있음)을 짚고 있어서, 학습자가 옮겨 말할 text 의 "sitting straight up in a row" 를 짚도록 고쳤다.
